passage:
Ishita: hey, did you post the "wheat shortage" message in the building group?
Aditi: yes! my cousin forwarded it, said shops will run out by tonight 😰
Ishita: it's fake, the food office says stocks are normal. Everyone's rushing to the stores
Aditi: oh no. I also wrote that Gupta Stores is hiding stock
Ishita: yeah, Mr Gupta's shop was mobbed and he's upset
Aditi: I feel sick. Deleting it now.
Aditi: Posted in the group: "Correction: my earlier message was false. Stocks are normal. Sorry for the panic."
Aditi: I'm going to his shop to apologise in person
Ishita: good. Maybe check before forwarding next time?
Aditi: from now on I check first, forward second 🙂

qa.q: What did Aditi's message say about Gupta Stores?
qa.a: It said Gupta Stores is hiding stock.

qa.q: How was Aditi feeling when Ishita said Mr Gupta's shop had been mobbed?
qa.a: Aditi felt sick and guilty, and moved straight to delete the message.

qa.q: What did Aditi do to repair the harm, and what would help in future?
qa.a: Aditi deleted the message, posted a correction in the same group and went to apologise in person. Checking before forwarding would help in future.

qa.q: How might Mr Gupta have experienced the false message?
qa.a: He was upset, since a crowd mobbed his shop because of a rumour naming it. An apology face to face may help him feel the record is straight.

grounding: Sharing a false message causes panic and hurts someone named; delete, correct to the same audience, apologise, and check before sharing.
